newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends banner week mostly higher in US.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends banner week mostly higher in US.

text.p: *Dlr ends near highs vs yen, strong vs Swiss franc, while holding on to solid overseas gains on mark. Unwinding of short mark cross positions allow dollar to broaden gains.
*Dealers eye 1.8430 dollar/mark, 117 dollar/yen resistance levels.
*Buba's Jochimsen, Gaddum remarks keep dollar/mark honest.
*US Q2 ECI due Tues, Q2 GDP due Thurs, July jobs and NAPM Fri.
The dollar ended an impressive week broadly higher on Friday, padding gains made overseas amid continued unwinding of short mark cross positions.
After setting another six-year peak of 1.8403 marks in European dealings, the greenback stabilized and stuck to tight ranges against the German currency for much of the U.S. session.
But it leapt higher against the Swiss franc, setting a near four-year top of 1.5182, and pushed up to two-month highs against the yen.

"We've seen more unwinding of short mark crosses, which has kept dollar/mark somewhat stable at the higher end of its range, but has allowed the dollar to go up against many other currencies," said Stephen Flanagan, vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Credit Agricole Indosuez.
The dollar closed at 1.8368/78 marks, little changed from its opening rate of 1.8370/75. It rose to a peak of 116.99 yen, before settling at 116.82/92 against 116.05/15 at the outset of trading.
However, for a second day in a row, the dollar's most impressive gains came at the expense of the Swiss franc.
Helped by another substantial rise in the mark/Swiss cross, the dollar closed at 1.5155/65 francs, up from 1.5135/45 at the open and a full centime above Thursday's ending rate of 1.5053/63.
"It opens up the door for more moves higher to catch up to dollar/mark," said Russell LaScala, chief dealer at Citibank.

The dollar gleaned mild support on Friday from a Commerce Department report which showed that orders for durable goods rose a heady 2.3 percent in June -- much higher than Wall Street economists had expected.
But remarks from several Bundesbank members and news of a 2.6 percent decline in purchases of existing homes during June kept dollar gains in check during the U.S. session, dealers said.

Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum was quoted in a European weekly newspaper on Friday as saying the dollar was slightly overvalued against the mark, but that mark weakness was not sparking inflationary pressures in Germany.

Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen told a German daily that central bank policymakers were "driving carefully" in the current exchange rate environment, and suggested the Bundesbank wanted to send a signal to the market by setting its repo rate at a fixed level for only a portion of the current recess period.
"The Bundesbank has definitely added an element of caution to the market," said Flanagan.
Nevertheless, dealers expressed confidence that the dollar could continue to appreciate in the coming week -- a week which will include a heavy dose of key U.S. data.
On Tuesday, the Labor Department will release its Employment Cost Index for the second quarter, an important gauge of inflation pressures.

Other key indicators next week include an advanced reading of second quarter gross domestic product (GDP) on Thursday and the employment and National Association of Purchasing Management reports for the month of July on Friday.

Key levels to watch will be the 117 threshold in dollar/yen and the 1.8430 target in dollar/mark, dealers said. Decisive breaks of these key technical hurdles could open the flood gates for further dollar rallies.
In other trade on Friday, the British pound ended at $1.6645/55, up slightly from $1.6640/50 at the open, while the Australian dollar edged up to $0.7377.82 from $0.7373/78.

The dollar climbed to Canadian $1.3843/48 from an opening rate of C$1.3819/24 and ended slightly lower at 6.1905/35 French francs after roaring to a six-year peak of 6.2022 francs in European dealings.
(( -- Noah Barkin, N.A. Forex Unit, 212-859-1673 ))
